newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee higher, London seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee higher, London seen easing.

text.p: Indonesian coffee prices were higher on Monday on continued talk of tight supply as rumours emerged of possible shipment delays, traders said.
They said London's benchmark September futures contract was due to open unchanged to $10-$20 lower later on Monday.
"There has been talk of possible shipments' delays because of the increase in local bean prices over the past few weeks," one trader said. "But to-date there has been no confirmation."
"It can happen because the discount between the local free-on-board (FOB) price and the London price has shrunk considerable from around $200-$250 several weeks ago."

Traders said grade four robusta was quoted at 4,000-4,100 rupiah/kg in Lampung in south Sumatra, compared with 3,800-3,850 rupiah a kg a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,600-$1,650 a tonne against $1,630.
They said some players were offering beans at as high as $1,700-$1,750, compared with London's September contract closing level of $1,795 last Friday.
"Some players are offering at very strange levels," another trader said, referring to the export prices. "They are trying to exaggerate the supply tightness in the local market."
"Of course, their quotes are the starting points for negotiations with buyers," he added.
The trader said some collectors, who form the link between farmers and exporters, were storing beans at exporters' warehouses for future sales.
"They are just storing truckloads of beans at the warehouses without fixing the price," he said. "They will negotiate the price with exporters when they feel the price is right."
Another trader said collectors and farmers did not seem to be in a rush to sell their beans as there were no festivals or occasions that needed expenditure at the moment.
"Other than having to spend on school items when their children head back to school after the holidays next week, they do not seem to need extra cash," he added.
"So, they are in a position to hold on to their coffee at the moment," he added.
